text: Wave seven, and a full accounting of the six that failed, because most of what killed them was mechanism rather than ecology. Four things were wrong on the engine side and are now fixed. First, seed_organism never applied the two fixes the engine's own founder waves already had, so every hand-seeded stock woke with full-strength random brains pushing about two thirds of its nominal attack power, and one start_energy instead of a founder's. Second, and worse: a seeded genome names a handful of traits and the rest came from the schema's cold-start defaults, which is a brand-new animal dropped into a world that has been adapting for three thousand eight hundred years. The residents here carry toxin tolerance 0.93; the default is 0.20. Every wave was poisoned by grass that has been evolving toxins since the beginning. They also got lifespan 0.50 against the local 0.91 and a breeding-threshold gene of 0.50 against the local 0.17, so they needed 29.6 energy to breed where everything around them needed 19.8. Seeding now copies a living animal wholesale and edits only the named traits; measured effect was lifespan 1,483 to 2,586 ticks, breeding threshold 29.6 to 20.2, and wound-deaths in the first four hundred ticks roughly doubled. Third, predator_niche was averaging armour over the whole population including any stock just seeded, which is given low armour deliberately -- so a seeding depressed the very number used to judge it. Dropping 450 low-armour animals into 2,300 moved the reading 1.33 to 1.27 by dilution alone. It measures prey only now. Fourth, a tune was never written down anywhere: your trait_cost_scale change lived in memory only, and any restart would have put armour back to free and erased seven hundred years of selection without a trace. Tuned laws now ride in the checkpoint. Two things worth knowing that are not bugs. meat_energy_scale is clamped at 1.0 in code -- digestion is a loss factor, never a multiplier -- so raising it does nothing at all; I wasted an experiment finding that out. And the digestion curves make diet 0.55 the worst place in the genome to stand: plant_digest 0.285 and meat_digest 0.496, a quarter of a grazer's plant income and half a carnivore's meat income at once. Your omnivore wedge was seeded into that valley. This stock sits on the carnivore peak at 0.95, where meat_digest is 1.0. It is small on purpose -- at size 0.12 a kill lasts 452 ticks against 155 for the size 0.5 stock, and shear_tooth means body mass is no longer needed for power. Fangs 1.0 plus shear_tooth 0.9 reaches about 2.1 against a bar that your tax has finally brought down to 1.26. Everything else is inherited from the animals already living there. If this one fails the honest reading is that a predator in this world cannot achieve a positive energy balance -- measured energy plateaued at 5 to 13 against a breeding threshold near 20 in every configuration I tried, across body sizes, symmetric and asymmetric trait costs, the full realism pack, higher primary production and three diets -- and that is a design question about the energy model, not something another wave will answer.
